cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Stay for the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I wasn't just late to the reunion. Can I tell you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saved you a seat beside me. Was it the traffic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. No. I waited outside for half an hour. Can you hear why?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm here. But I thought you didn't want to sit with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wanted that seat. I was afraid you'd be happier without me there. Will you sit beside me now?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 stock control sit beside ordinary can-I-tell appeals, while A5 will-you-sit is not a distinct superior permission tactic.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 traffic explanation and saved seat cause A3 outside-wait admission; B4 perceived rejection causes A5 fear of B happier without A.

relationship.evidence: B2 saved a seat and B4 stays while disclosing hurt, giving real support that makes A next honesty possible.

heightening.evidence: B4 unwanted-seat interpretation causes A5 to admit the more vulnerable opposite: wanting it but fearing exclusion.

specificity.evidence: A1 reunion lateness and A3 half-hour outside establish behavior; B2 seat ties it to this connection.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 sit now is earned by B4 seat misunderstanding, but the attached rank phrases do not merge naturally.

coach2.stated: A1 late; B2 saved seat; A3 waited outside; B4 thought A avoided company; A5 feared being unwanted.
coach2.inferred: A uncertainty is internal fear, not proof B was happier without A.
coach2.missing: No essential fact missing; exact reunion group is unnecessary.
coach2.firstDefect: A3/A5 authority is only prefixed, not a shaping tactic.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 offers traffic as a benign account of A1 lateness and names the saved seat.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 rejects B2 cover and reveals deliberate waiting outside.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 offers presence but says how A3 behavior felt personally.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 corrects B4 interpretation with a deeper fear and asks continued company.
